verdict_reason: My round-5 YELLOW rested on exactly one thing -- isotropy.py computing the mean AND the centring in the INPUT dtype and only then promoting, which cost IsoScore the translation invariance it has by definition. That is fixed (isotropy.py:268-269 now does `Xd = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64); Xc = Xd - Xd.mean(...)`) and I re-ran my own counterexample: a float32 4096x8 exactly-balanced integer cloud now returns 0.997900285531 at offsets 0, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 AND 1e7 -- bit-identical at every offset, against the released IsoScore 2.0.1's 0.997900285636 -- where the round-5 code collapsed to 0.001783276461 at 1e6 (-99.8%). Nothing else has to change. Rudman et al. Table 2's closed form iota(I_9^(k)) = (k-1)/8 is reproduced for all nine k on exactly-orthonormalised k-of-9 clouds with worst absolute error 2.220e-16. Against the authors' released IsoScore 2.0.1 executed locally in its documented (num_samples, dimension) orientation, the worst absolute disagreement over six clouds is 3.806e-08 (isotropic 1000x8 5.990e-10, isotropic 500x64 6.049e-09, N<d 20x100 2.020e-08, anisotropic 300x16 3.806e-08, rank-3 400x12 6.858e-09, clustered 600x32 1.454e-08) -- float32 inside the released torch path, not a formula gap. Scale invariance holds across the full contract ladder: the same float32 cloud reads 0.997900285468 to 0.997900285593 over 1e-30 ... 1e+30, a spread of 1.3e-10. I found no remaining value-changing counterexample. ADJUDICATION: on this code state the measurement supports the round-5 codex GREEN over my own round-5 YELLOW; codex's round-5 verdict was written against the already-fixed kernel and mine against the pre-fix one.
comparable_reason: Eq. 4.1 carries an exact structural 1/(d-1), so a model that genuinely uses k dimensions scores lower purely for being wider. Direct intervention: one fixed 2000x8 cloud zero-padded to d = 8/16/64/512/4096 -- an exact isometry that changes nothing about the geometry -- moves the raw score 0.993307287626 -> 0.463543400892 -> 0.110367476403 -> 0.013606949146 -> 0.001697961175, a factor of 585, while `isoscore_effective_dims` stays at 7.953151013385 to the last printed digit at ALL FIVE widths. Across the 51 archived study models whose configs resolve, raw isoscore has Spearman -0.4753 with d_model (p = 4.24e-04), -0.3825 with n_layers (p = 5.61e-03), -0.3489 with vocab_size (p = 1.21e-02) and -0.4623 with parameter count (p = 1.76e-04, n = 61). Only `isoscore_effective_dims` belongs in a cross-width feature matrix -- and note it is algebraically the covariance participation ratio, i.e. the same quantity geometry_svd emits as `participation_ratio`, so the two must not both enter a sparse selection.
github_reason: Read the released `IsoScore.IsoScore.IsoScore` source (torch.cov(points.T) -> torch.linalg.svdvals -> pcs*sqrt(n)/||pcs|| -> defect/sqrt(2(n - sqrt n)) -> the Eq. 4.1 rescale) and executed it head to head with BLME's `_isoscore` on six clouds. NOTE ON ORIENTATION: the released signature takes (num_samples, dimension) and reads `n = points.shape[1]`; passing the transpose (as an earlier reconstruction of this comparison did) silently makes n the SAMPLE count and builds an N x N covariance -- a 1000x8 isotropic cloud then scores 0.0059 instead of 0.988 and takes 86 s. In the correct orientation the worst absolute disagreement is 3.806e-08. I then used the same package as the arbiter for the translation case: it holds 0.997900285636 at every offset while BLME now holds 0.997900285531 at every offset, so the round-5 divergence is closed.
paper_reason: Rudman, Gillman, Rayne & Eickhoff (arXiv:2108.07344) Table 2 publishes iota(I_9^(k)) = (k-1)/8 for k = 1..9: 0.000, 0.125, 0.250, 0.375, 0.500, 0.625, 0.750, 0.875, 1.000. Driving exactly-orthonormalised k-of-9 clouds (SVD-orthonormalised so the covariance spectrum is exactly k ones and 9-k zeros, then randomly rotated) through BLME's kernel returns 0.000000000000000, 0.125000000000000, 0.250000000000000, 0.375000000000000, 0.500000000000000, 0.625000000000000, 0.750000000000000, 0.875000000000000, 1.000000000000000 -- worst absolute error 2.220e-16 (k = 4 and k = 8), i.e. all nine published values to machine precision.
confounds_reason: For the RAW score, confirmed with a known mechanism: the 1/(d-1) factor in Eq. 4.1, demonstrated by a zero-padding isometry that moves the value 585x with the geometry held fixed, and by Spearman -0.4753 with d_model (p = 4.24e-04) and -0.4623 with parameter count (p = 1.76e-04) over the archived zoo. The named twin removes that channel: recomputing isoscore*(d-1)+1 on the same archived records takes rho(d_model) -0.4753 -> -0.1662 (p = 0.244), rho(n_layers) -0.3825 -> -0.1617 (p = 0.257) and rho(params) -0.4623 -> -0.2697 (p = 0.056). The one channel it does NOT remove is vocabulary, -0.3489 -> -0.3407 (p = 0.0144) -- but vocabulary is essentially a family label in this zoo and the association is present in the raw score at the same strength, so the twin is not relocating a width effect; it is leaving a family effect alone. That distinction is why `normalized_ok` is GREEN and `confounds` is CONFIRMED at the same time.
